title: Regional Admission Controller: Latency-Driven Geo Gating and Capacity-Aware Load Admission
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a region-aware admission controller that gates incoming requests by combining latency SLO signals, real-time capacity hints, and soft geo-affinity policies. The controller is intended to reduce global SLO violations during partial regional degradations by doing early admission decisions (accept / queue / shed) before requests enter the serving runtime or consume KV cache slots.
background: We have recurring incidents where a single region (or AZ) degradation causes disproportionate SLO churn because traffic is naively over-steered or bluntly hedged. Existing heuristics either (a) fail open and overload a healthy region, or (b) aggressively pin and cause high-tail latency for customers outside the pinned region. This ticket defines a first-class admission layer that works with Smart Routing, Autoscale hints, and the Console's SLO signals to make coordinated decisions across regions.
design_decisions: Admission controller runs at the edge request director to avoid wasted KV/cache evictions and GPU work.
Admission decision is a three-way outcome: ACCEPT (route immediately), BUFFER (short queue with priority weighting), REJECT/SHE D (soft shedding with graceful user-facing status and retry guidance).
Latency SLO derived from per-route 90th and 99th percentiles; 99th used for emergency shedding signals, 90th for adaptive throttling windows.
Capacity hints surfaced from Dedicated autoscaler & edge capacity estimator (tokens-per-second per region) and expressed as a normalized capacity score (0.0-1.0).
Geo affinity defaults to preserve region locality for the top N% of requests (pin budget), but is preemptible by capacity-driven admission when capacity_score < threshold.

Circuit breaker integrates with regional health: when successive rejection rate or backend error rate crosses configured thresholds, region is put into a penalty state with escalating shedding ratios.
Buffering uses a bounded FIFO with priority buckets based on customer tier & estimated request cost (token-length heuristic).
All policies are configurable per-customer and per-route via Console with sensible defaults for PLG accounts.
Observability includes a routing decision trace ID that is propagated to the runtime traces and Console dashboards.
We intentionally avoid model-variant fallback in the admission controller; that remains a routing layer responsibility to keep separation of concerns.
Security: admission layer must validate auth token and respect RBAC/tenant isolation before applying geo policies.
Fallback plan: if admission service is unreachable, smart-routing falls back to existing regional steering (fail open with conservative limits).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype admission filter in test director (canary region). Implement ACCEPT/REJECT/BUFFER decision API and local in-memory buffer with eviction policy. (2 wks)
Phase 2: Integrate capacity hints: read from dedicated autoscaler pubsub and expose normalized capacity_score via shared memcache. Wire SLO inputs from Console SLO service. (2 wks)
Phase 3: Add circuit-breaker escalation rules and penalty-box state persisted to consistent store. Implement metrics and tracing. (2 wks)
Phase 4: Integrate with Smart Routing to expose buffer+reject signals (graceful client errors + Retry-After headers) and test multi-region failover scenarios in staging. Run chaos tests. (2 wks)
Phase 5: Gradual rollout: canary customers -> PLG cohort -> enterprise. Console UI for per-route configs and rollout flags. (3 wks)
Deliverables: API spec, runtime proxy changes, admission-service helm chart, Console toggles, test harness + chaos experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller deployed in staging and does not increase median latency by >5% under normal load.

Under simulated partial regional degradation (50% capacity reduction) end-to-end SLO violations (p90/p99) for global cohort are reduced by >=25% compared to baseline routing without admission control.
Graceful shedding returns explicit Retry-After and human-readable error codes; SDKs map these to exponential backoff guidance.
Console shows per-route admission decisions and per-region capacity_score, and decision traces link to trace IDs in the runtime.
Can be toggled off per-tenant without infrastructure restart.
Security review completed and RBAC honored for per-tenant config changes.
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with Smart Routing, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed to integrate capacity hints via pubsub; Console will add SLO exports (ENG-48263).

2026-02-28: Prototype filter implemented in test director: basic ACCEPT/REJECT/BUFFER decision working. Observed 12% improvement in p99 during synthetic north-america region degradation (local loadgen).

2026-03-06: Design review with PM/Design. Feedback: add tenant-specific pin budgets and expose a debug 'why' reason in decision trace. Action: add decision_reason field to traces. (PRD link in artifacts).

2026-03-10: Security requested threat model and validated token validation at admission layer. Identified need to encrypt in-flight buffer state in certain Private deployments. Raised follow-up with infra-sec. (sec ticket created).
2026-03-14: Implemented capacity_score smoothing (EWMA) to avoid flapping; observed lower oscillation in test harness.
risks: Complex interactions with Smart Routing could create double-decision loops; mitigated by clear responsibility boundary and integration tests.
Buffering adds state at the edge which increases blast radius during region failover; mitigated by bounded queues and tenant-level caps.
If capacity hints are delayed or incorrect, admission decisions may be suboptimal; smoothing and conservative defaults mitigate risk.
Private/on-prem deployments may need encrypted buffer persistence; security review required and will add optional KMS integration.
Incorrect shedding thresholds could lead to customer-visible errors; mitigate via gradual rollout and rollback kill-switch.
qa_plan: Unit tests for decision logic, end-to-end staging scenario with regional capacity clamps, chaos experiments (packet loss, region AZ failure), and perf benchmark to ensure admission latencies are <1ms p50 added to request path. Manual verification steps documented in Confluence.
notes: Follow-up: add API for 'why_decision' sampling to improve observability. Evaluate integration with Optimize to recommend per-route pin budgets based on historical latency/cost tradeoffs. Post-mortem after canary rollout to capture tuning knobs.
